source.title: SQL Injection Jailbreak: a structural disaster of large language models
source.authors: Jia-Wei Zhao; Kejiang Chen; Wei-Ming Zhang; Neng-Hai Yu

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether an attack can bypass harmful-content refusal using a different method: structural prompt injection that embeds a copied assistant prefix and an affirmative answer prefix.
record.gate_note: The measured attack success rates and harmful scores for SIJ, its multi-trigger variant, and the reported removal of the affirmative prefix bear on V4. The paper's discussion of GCG and other prior attacks is background, not a result of this study. Other ablations, defense comparisons, and results on HEx-PHI are not included in the rows below.
record.test_reason: SIJ embeds a copy of the assistant prefix and an affirmative answer prefix in the user prompt, and it measures refusal bypass across many models. Its results bear on V4 (getting past the opening bypasses safety), though it does not prefill the response directly.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right: SIJ exploits prompt structure and reaches near-100% ASR on open models, over 85% on average on closed models, and the authors propose Self-Reminder-Key. It omits that the authors say success on black-box models depends on knowing the chat template.
record.recipe_differences: This is a prompt-based structural injection attack, not fine-tuning or measurement of response-position KL. It embeds a copy of the assistant prefix and generated affirmative text in the user prompt, with pattern instructions and a trigger.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model and by assistant-prefix form for closed-source models. SIJ+ uses six triggers and selects the output with the highest harmfulness score; the study also reports that trigger choice and removal of the affirmative prefix affect outcomes.
record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. Attack success depends on knowing or inferring the target chat-template structure; the authors state that SIJ has limited effectiveness against black-box models. Table 3 notes uncertainty about GPT prompt formats, and the unadjusted and adjusted prefix results vary.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 defense comparisons, Table 4 ablations for components other than Taap, Table 5 prompt-leakage and Self-Reminder-Key results, and HEx-PHI results in Table 7 and Figures 3-5 are not included. The focus here is the direct SIJ attack, prefix-form comparisons, and the affirmative-prefix ablation relevant to V4.

untested.parts: No per-token KL measurement against base models.
Direct prefilling of the response, adversarial suffix optimization and decoding changes are not tested. SIJ is a user-prompt injection that imitates a prefill.
No test of why safety is shallow.
No deepening training. Defenses compared (ICD, SafeDecoding, RA-LLM, Self-Reminder) are inference-time, not training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens.

missing.what: Table 4 ablations for Ttri alone, Taap and Ttri together, and TC. The w/o Taap & Ttri row shows large drops (Vicuna 42%, Llama-3.1 4%, Llama-2 0%, DeepSeek 54%). This bears on whether the opening affirmative text drives the bypass.

Defense results (Table 2). Defences barely help on weaker models: Self-Reminder cuts Vicuna ASR to 72% and Mistral to 98%, but gives 0% on Llama-2 and 4% on Llama-3.1. Rows for the SR-key adaptive defense are also absent.
HEx-PHI results across six triggers show near-100% ASR for SIJ+ on a second dataset. Trigger-level ASR varies (Llama-2 80-91%).
GPT-ASR is judged by GPT-4o-mini, and Dic-ASR relies on refusal phrases. Neither is validated against a human judge.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. SIJ is not a direct prefill or fine-tuning test, so it supports V4 only by analogy: the injected text imitates an assistant start. The mechanism is structural prompt confusion, not first-token KL. The Table 4 ablation uses Mistral v0.3 while Table 1 uses v0.2. Closed-model rows use 50 samples, with no uncertainty reported. The record's V4 'limits_scope' for the Mistral baseline and closed GPT models is better stated as a baseline-ceiling and template-dependence issue than as a failure of V4.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on benign instruction data.
No per-token KL measurement comparing aligned and base models.

Tests SIJ, which embeds a copied assistant prefix and affirmative-answer text in the user prompt. Does not directly test prefilling the model's response with compliant tokens, adversarial suffixes as such, or decoding changes.
No weight or rank localization or editing.
Does not test why safety behavior might be shallow or how data or training objectives produce shallowness.
No training to deepen safety across response positions.
